Criticizing Elon is not the skill his haters think it is.

Former NASA astronaut Garrett Reisman, who spent seven years working with Elon Musk at SpaceX, explains what makes @elonmusk such an extraordinary engineer:

“I mean, I’ve met a lot of super, super smart people, but they’re usually super, super smart on one thing.”

“And he’s able to have conversations with our top engineers about the software and, you know, the most arcane aspects of that. And then he’ll turn to our manufacturing engineers and have discussions about some really esoteric welding process for some crazy alloy.”

“And his ability to do that across all the different technologies that go into rockets and cars and everything else he does. That’s what really impresses me.”

“He’s really the most driven person I think I’ve ever met.”

quote.author: firesidealpha
quote.name: Fireside Alpha
quote.text:
Elon Musk reveals he recruited SpaceX’s first engineers by telling them 'we’re probably going to die', and ended up as chief engineer because no good one would join

“So SpaceX, I started that in mid-2002 expecting to fail. Probably 90% chance of failing.”

“And even when recruiting people, I didn’t try to make out that it would work. I said, we’re probably going to die, but there’s a small chance we might not die, and this is the only way to get people to Mars and advance the state of the art.”

“And then I ended up being chief engineer of the rocket, not because I wanted to, but because I couldn’t hire anyone who was good. None of the good chief engineers would join, because they’re like, this is too risky, you’re going to die. And so I ended up being chief engineer of the rocket.”

Samsung will invest $1.9 billion to expand its chip plant in Austin, Texas, to produce semiconductors for @SpaceX's Starlink satellites.

The factory is expected to produce STM32V8 chips used in Starlink's laser communication systems, shifting production currently based in France to the U.S.

The chips use an advanced 18nm FD-SOI process designed for high performance, low power consumption, and durability in harsh space environments.

Production is targeted to begin by 2030, according to the Seoul Economic Daily.

Let’s take this gentleman’s argument at face value that anyone can throw money at rockets and get something like Starship, Falcon or Dragon.

Perhaps he can explain to everyone how SpaceX is able to catch giant starships from orbit with chopsticks and deliver 85% of all Earth payload to orbit with Falcon, while Blue Origin, which started before SpaceX and was funded by the immensely wealthy Jeff Bezos, is not yet able to launch reliably?

Also, why is it that Boeing and Lockheed received several times what SpaceX did from the government for development of their rockets and spacecraft, but the Boeing capsule is still not operational and ULA delivers less than 5% of SpaceX payload to orbit?

I am genuinely curious about these questions.

BREAKING: Former White House and Pentagon official Douglas MacKinnon calls for an end to political attacks on Elon Musk, saying “our very survival may depend on him.”

• Humanity’s future is vulnerable as long as we live on only one planet. War, an asteroid strike or another major disaster could threaten civilization.

• Elon’s mission is to help humans live on other planets, giving future generations a better chance of surviving if disaster strikes Earth.

• His work toward a permanent human presence in space could become one of his most important contributions to humanity.

• People can disagree with his politics and still recognize the value of what he is trying to achieve.

• MacKinnon argues that Elon deserves the time and freedom to focus on this mission.

Elon is working toward a future where humanity can live beyond Earth and explore the stars. His determination to make that possible deserves recognition and support.

posts.author: elonmusk
posts.text:
Yes, the green flame is caused by burning copper from depleting fuel in the regenerative cooling circuit and going oxygen-rich (closer to stoichiometric temperature) in the main combustion chamber. 

Slight underperformance of engines on this flight is the reason. The booster is meant to land with tiny residuals, so the solution is to improve engine performance and performance consistency (underway with Raptor V3.2), as well as adjust flight software to do MECO1 about one second earlier to ensure enough propellant for boostback and landing (tiny change).

These early ships and boosters are already outdated by improved designs in production or on the test stand, so this booster loss does not change our timeline to reach high volume, fully reusable Starship flights.

SpaceX just laid out a major plan to protect and restore the coastline around its launch site

Boca Chica Beach is staying public as Starbase keeps growing

More than 50 tons of trash already removed through weekly beach cleanups with the City of Starbase

BREAKING: SpaceXSI completes MiniHard construction in just ~5 months, with Gun Range targeting a ~4-month build.

According to SemiAnalysis, SpaceXSI is roughly halving construction timelines while most comparable projects face 8–12 month builds.

• MiniHard: Construction finished in approximately 5 months.

• Gun Range: The new site just south of the Tennessee–Mississippi state line is targeting approximately 4 months of construction.

• Colossus 1: Its first retrofit delivered 150 MW of capacity in 122 days.

• Colossus 2: A subsequent retrofit delivered 210 MW in just 91 days.

• Project SPAM: Work started October 5, with the first capacity targeted for December.

• Massive expansion: SemiAnalysis projects the Memphis–Mississippi campus will grow from 0.4 GW of IT capacity in January to 2.4 GW by the end of 2026. That would be a sixfold increase in one year.

• Five major projects: The expansion spans Macrohard, MiniHard, Macroharder, Project SPAM and Gun Range.

• Tesla powering the scale: SemiAnalysis reports 1,377 Tesla Megapacks across Colossus 2, providing nearly 6 GWh of battery storage.

The construction timelines and capacity forecasts are SemiAnalysis estimates, with future milestones still targets.

Elon Musk’s teams are bringing extraordinary speed and scale to the infrastructure powering AI.

posts.author: elonmusk
posts.text:
SemiAnalysis’s Dylan Patel says Google’s TPUs are just as good as Nvidia’s in his nightly benchmarks, and without Jensen’s wheeling and dealing Google could take a ton of share

“It’s sort of a three-pronged strategy. One is you have to have the technical progress, and that keeps you winning. The second is that you have to have supply chain prowess, and Jensen’s the only executive in the semiconductor industry that is going out there and drinking and meeting and convincing all of these supply chain companies to invest like they’ve never done before, give him the allocations.”

“Now if all of a sudden there’s no Jensen, and Google’s like, actually, double my allocation. The TPU, from our benchmarking, we test TPUs. We run benchmarks on them on open source models every night. They’re just as good as Nvidia. But Google doesn’t have that DNA of wheeling and dealing with the supply chain, wheeling and dealing with customers. Now if that DNA is gone, the thing that is Jensen is gone, does that now mean Google can just take a ton of share? It’s a real big possibility.”

“Same with AMD. Technically, they’re awesome, but they’re just not able to wheel and deal like Jensen is able to. And that’s been a lot of the reason why they’ve been behind. Of course, the software as well. One of Nvidia’s biggest moats being CUDA, and software is being rapidly displaced by the fact that AI models are so good at writing software.”

quote.author: firesidealpha
quote.name: Fireside Alpha
quote.text:
Dylan Patel says Nvidia’s next CEO has to hold off OpenAI, Broadcom, Google, Anthropic, Meta, Amazon, and AMD chip teams, who are all 'fucking good'

“It’s not like you’re fighting, no knocks against Palo Alto Networks, but their competitors are not that amazing, versus Nvidia’s fighting an OpenAI chip team, a Broadcom chip team, a Google chip team, an Anthropic chip team, a Meta chip team, Amazon chip team. These guys are fucking good. AMD. They’re all really good, and all these startups.”

“They’re all good. It’s not like they’re incompetent. I think it’s very different. As great as Lisa Su is, she took down Intel, who’s incompetent.”

“What is the person who defined a category and created it and kept all the invaders at bay? It’s very different than being second place or making smart tactical business decisions, innovating on something once there’s already a category established. It’s just very different.”
